cards.explanation: The answer is washing them with water. God tells Moses, Israel's leader, to present Aaron and his sons at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water (Exodus 29:4). The washing comes first. The garments and the oil come after. Even I wipe the flour off my face before I put the good hat on.

The answer is False. God calls the priesthood a permanent statute for Aaron and his sons (Exodus 29:9), so it isn't limited to their own lifetimes. He backs that up when He says the holy garments will belong to Aaron's sons after him (Exodus 29:29). That's a long line of hats getting passed down, friends.

The answer is True. God says that when the young bull is presented at the front of the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head (Exodus 29:10). The same step comes up again with both rams (Exodus 29:15, 19). Three animals, three sets of hands on heads. Those priests' hands are going to be busy.

The answer is sin. God has the young bull's fat burned on the altar, and the flesh, hide and dung burned outside the camp. Then He names it Himself: “it is a sin offering.” (Exodus 29:14) He doesn't leave us guessing, and I like a recipe that tells you what you're making.

The answer is a pleasing aroma to Him. God says the whole first ram is burned on the altar as “…a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.” (Exodus 29:18) The phrase comes straight from His own words. I smell a good batch from the oven, but this is a whole different level.

The answer is that it consecrates them and their garments. When Moses sprinkles the blood from the altar and the anointing oil on Aaron, his sons and their garments, God says, “Then he and his garments will be consecrated, as well as his sons and their garments.” (Exodus 29:21) Notice that the clothes get included too, friends. Mine just get flour.

The answer is waved. God says the ordination ram's fat, thigh, loaf, cake and wafer go into the hands of Aaron and his sons, and they “…wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.” (Exodus 29:24) Hands full, arms moving, all of it done before the LORD. I get tired just carrying one full tray of cookies across my bakery, so I'm impressed.

The answer is False. God says, “This will belong to Aaron and his sons as a regular portion from the Israelites…” (Exodus 29:28) Regular means it keeps happening, so it isn't a one-time gift for ordination day. The text calls it the heave offering the Israelites make to the LORD from their peace offerings.

The answer is so his sons can be ordained in them. Aaron's holy garments go to his sons after him, and God says the reason is so they can be anointed and ordained in them (Exodus 29:29). Same clothes, next set of priests. I'd hand my apron down too, friends, but by now it's mostly flour.

The answer is because these things are sacred. God says no outsider may eat the ordination meat and bread “…because these things are sacred.” (Exodus 29:33) The same word shows up again in verse 34 about leftovers. Sacred is what decides who eats and what's done with the remains.

The answer is holy. After seven days of atonement for the altar, God says, “Then the altar will become most holy; whatever touches the altar will be holy.” (Exodus 29:37) Most holy is what He calls it, friends.

The answer is that He will meet and speak. God says the daily burnt offering will be made at the entrance to the tent for the generations to come, “…where I will meet you to speak with you.” (Exodus 29:42) The LORD says He will meet and speak there.

The answer is True. God says, “So I will consecrate the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.” (Exodus 29:44) Right after that He says, “Then I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.” (Exodus 29:45) He also says He brought them out of Egypt “…so that I might dwell among them.” (Exodus 29:46) God Himself says He will live among His people.

The answer is so He might dwell among them. God says He brought the Israelites out of Egypt “…so that I might dwell among them.” (Exodus 29:46) The whole passage leads to that, friends. Then He ends it with, “…I am the LORD their God.”
